title: Violations of Environmental Public Health Act by Food Courts
what_it_is: Violations of Environmental Public Health Act by Food Courts

sections.label: NEA licenses food retail establishments
sections.summary: NEA licenses over 37,000 food retail establishments to ensure food sold is prepared hygienically and safe.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) currently licenses more than 37,000 food retail establishments, including restaurants, food kiosks, caterers and food stalls within hawker centres, coffee shops and food courts, to ensure that the food sold is prepared hygienically and safe for consumption.

sections.label: Inspections, enforcement and food poisoning rates
sections.summary: NEA inspections and enforcement actions rose from 2013 to 2016, while food poisoning incidence stayed at or below 3.2 outbreaks per 1,000 establishments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In 2016, NEA carried out more than 148,000 inspections and over 3,200 enforcement actions were taken against food retail establishments, an increase from around 2,500 in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Correspondingly, the number of licences that were suspended increased from 62 in 2013 to 132 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Meanwhile, the food poisoning incidence rate at food retail establishments had remained low, being consistently maintained at 3.2 food poisoning outbreaks per 1,000 food retail establishments or below since 2013.

sections.label: Food handlers hygiene course requirement
sections.summary: NEA requires all food handlers to attend and pass a basic food hygiene course and a refresher course.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: First, NEA currently requires all food handlers, that is, those who prepare or handle food, to attend and pass a basic food hygiene course, as well as a refresher course to ensure sustained awareness of food hygiene practices.

sections.label: Food Hygiene Officer scheme requirements
sections.summary: Restaurants of a certain size, food courts, canteens and caterers must appoint a trained senior staff member as a Food Hygiene Officer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Additionally, as I have said earlier, we have an FHO scheme, and restaurants of a certain size as well as food courts, canteens, caterers, are required to appoint a senior staff, a supervisor or operations manager, and even the sous chef, to be trained and appointed as FHOs so that they are responsible for implementing and ensuring good food hygiene practices as well as supervision, and ensuring that their other workers also comply.

sections.label: No mandatory BFHC for other workers
sections.summary: The view is that registering or mandating BFHC for all other workers is not necessary, except for food handlers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: At this point, our view is that it is not necessary to register or mandate BFHC for all other workers, except the food handlers, where there is really no direct impact on food safety as well as public health.

sections.label: Including sharing in training sessions
sections.summary: The speaker says it is a good idea and will make sure it is part of training sessions and sharings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I would assume that under the syllabus when the lecturers do this training, that could have already been shared.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But having said that, I think that it is a good idea and I will make sure this is part of the training sessions and sharings.
